name: ALPS
summary: The ALPS series searches for axions and other light bosons with light shining through a wall; ALPS II uses long magnet strings and precision optical resonators.
detection_principle: Laser photons convert to weakly coupled particles in a magnetic field, pass through an opaque wall and convert back to photons, read out by heterodyne or single-photon detection.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design

key_parameters.name: ALPS II
key_parameters.value: Magnet strings exceeding 100 m on each side of the wall

results.summary: The first science run found no new bosons; later optical upgrades are expected to improve sensitivity.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
